chunks: The least number of days of menstruation (al-hayd) is three, and the maximum of it is ten days. The least number of purity is ten days, and its maximum has no limit. The maximum number of days of the woman in post-partum bleeding (al-nifas) in which she refrains from prayer is eighteen days, and she waits a day or two unless she is purified prior to that.

key_terms.الحيض: Hayd — menstrual bleeding, rendering a woman ritually impure
key_terms.الطهر: Tuhr — the interval of ritual purity between bleeding episodes
key_terms.تستظهر: Istizhar — the practice of cautionary waiting beyond the expected cessation of bleeding

ai.seo_question: What are the minimum and maximum days of menstruation and post-partum bleeding in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This text lays out the jurisprudential limits for three categories of female ritual bleeding: menstruation (hayd) ranges from three to ten days; the intervening purity period (tuhr) has a minimum of ten days but no upper limit; and post-partum bleeding (nifas) has a maximum of eighteen days during which prayer is suspended, with an additional one or two days of precautionary waiting unless purification occurs earlier. These rulings are foundational in Shia fiqh and reflect the Imam's teaching to distinguish obligatory rest from prayer from the woman's own assessment of her state of purity.
